svg.title: Module 12 one-page guide: Long-Running & Asynchronous Agents
svg.text: CSCI 391 · MODULE 12 · ONE-PAGE LECTURE GUIDE
Long-Running & Asynchronous Agents
Machines reboot, networks flap, APIs throttle, and users change their minds.
Part III · Architecture and Patterns · Week 12 · Read: Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 13
OPENING CASE
Monitor regulatory filings, cross-reference the product roadmap, produce a weekly briefing. On paper: 40 minutes. In
practice: throttling, retry storms, ~1,000 completions, $340, and nothing saved after the container recycled at hour
six.
Treat agent state as a first-class persistent artifact, not a transient
runtime variable.
KEY FRAMEWORK
Durable execution essentials
Checkpoint at named stages (the saga pattern)
Asynchronous task queues: pause, resume, cancel
Step-level cost accounting and budget kills
Heartbeats, progress reporting, and idempotency
YOU SHOULD BE ABLE TO
Externalize state to a durable store at well-defined
checkpoints
Design checkpoints that make resumed runs equal
continuous runs
Use idempotency so retries don't repeat side effects
Implement cancellation, heartbeats, scheduling, and
partial results
ENTERPRISE LENS · ADDISON BOYER
This is the saga pattern from distributed systems applied to agents: named stages, deterministic outputs,
persisted before moving on. You trade some flexibility for recoverability.
Checkpoints should carry operational metadata — wall-clock start, tokens so far, tool-call history, and the exact
model/temperature config.
Budget alarms belong in the run loop, not in next month's invoice.
DISCUSS
→ Which state must survive a process restart?
→ What should happen if a worker returns after its lease has expired?
Concepts after Caldwell, The Agentic AI Bible, Ch. 13. Case framing, synthesis, and enterprise lens: Addison Boyer.
